questions.q: In the Caldwell Precision Manufacturing kickoff, which process does the VP of Operations' request — getting Meridian back in under an hour when it goes down — map to?
options: Incident Management, built in Lesson 30
Knowledge Management, built in Lesson 31
Request Management, built in Lesson 31
Change Enablement, built in Lesson 30
questions.explain: Restoring a down service fast, even with a temporary workaround, is Incident Management's job.

questions.q: Why does this lesson treat the plant IT manager's 'stop the recurring Line 3 ticket' request as a different problem from the VP's 'fix Meridian faster' request?
options: Incident Management restores service fast with a workaround, while Problem Management investigates the permanent cause and is deliberately slower by design
They are actually the same request, just worded differently
Problem Management is only relevant to Change Enablement, not Incident
The Line 3 printer is not a real Configuration Item, so no process applies
questions.explain: Conflating these two is called out as the most common first-rollout mistake: one process optimizes for speed, the other for finding the real cause.

questions.q: Why does Meridian get its own risk-based Change path instead of the same generic approval process as every other system at Caldwell Precision?
options: Because it's the one business-critical system whose unreviewed change could stop shipments company-wide
Because Meridian changes never actually need approval
Because Standard changes are not allowed on any production system
Because the CFO requested it be excluded from Change Enablement entirely
questions.explain: The CFO's requirement is really a risk statement — Meridian's outsized business impact justifies scoped, risk-based approval rather than one blanket policy.

questions.q: Which stakeholder's request maps to Request Management, built in Lesson 31?
options: HR's request for a catalog item handling new-hire laptop and software access
The CFO's request for controlled Meridian changes
The VP of Operations' request for faster Priority 1 resolution
The plant IT manager's request about the Line 3 printer
questions.explain: Turning a manual, email-based onboarding process into a catalog item with tracked fulfillment is exactly what Request Management covers.

questions.q: What is the implicit sixth requirement this lesson identifies underneath the five stated stakeholder asks?
options: Measurable SLA commitments and a way to prove them, plus a self-service front door
A requirement to replace the Incident table with a custom table
A requirement to disable all manual Priority overrides platform-wide
A requirement to merge Incident and Problem into a single table
questions.explain: Nobody states it outright, but every stakeholder assumes IT can measure and prove its commitments — that's Service Level Management plus the Service Portal, both built in Lesson 31.
